question: Is It Safe to Enable Debug Mode on a Live WooCommerce Store?
metaDescription: Only with display turned off and logging to a private file — showing raw PHP errors to visitors exposes sensitive information and looks unprofessional.
shortAnswer: Enable logging, but never display, on a live store — setting WP_DEBUG_LOG to true writes errors to a private log file for later review, while keeping WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY false ensures visitors never see raw PHP errors on screen, which could expose file paths, database structure hints, or other information useful to an attacker, and looks unprofessional even when harmless.

image.alt: Debug logging enabled privately on a live store, while error display to visitors stays disabled to avoid exposing sensitive information

bodyHtml:
The Correct Live-Site Configuration

WordPress's debug settings are actually three separate, independently controllable options: WP_DEBUG (the master switch), WP_DEBUG_LOG (write errors to a file), and WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY (show errors on screen). The safe production configuration is debug on, logging on, but display off — this captures everything needed for troubleshooting in a private log file that only someone with server access can read, without ever exposing raw error output to actual site visitors.

define( 'WP_DEBUG', true );
define( 'WP_DEBUG_LOG', true );
define( 'WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY', false );

Why Display-On Is Genuinely Risky

  • Raw PHP errors can reveal server file paths, which is minor reconnaissance information for an attacker but information that shouldn't be freely given away regardless.
  • Database-related error messages can occasionally hint at table structure or query details, again minor on their own but unnecessary exposure.
  • It looks unprofessional and can alarm customers who happen to trigger an error and see a wall of technical text instead of a clean error page, potentially damaging trust at exactly the wrong moment (like during checkout).
  • Left on indefinitely, even logging-only debug mode can accumulate a very large log file over time on a busy site, worth monitoring and periodically clearing rather than leaving to grow unbounded.

Setting This Up Correctly

  1. Set the three debug constants in wp-config.php as shown above for safe, ongoing production logging.
  2. Periodically check and clear wp-content/debug.log to prevent it from growing unbounded.
  3. Only temporarily enable display (never left on) while actively debugging directly on a staging copy, never on live.
